description: The request form itself — the one component every request page in the system renders, in create, edit or read-only mode. Covers the field set, the shared option constants, S3 attachments, the workflow stepper, and the two ways out of the page: save as draft, or submit and enter the approval chain.

happy_path.result: an empty form; Requested By is pre-filled from the session and Position from the profile

happy_path.action: fills title, type, priority, details, justification, work scope
happy_path.result: fields validate on blur and re-validate on change once wrong
they are parked as pending uploads — nothing reaches S3 yet
attachments flush to S3, the request is created with masterStatus DRAFT, an audit log CREATED is written, and the browser goes to /requests/$requestId — the VIEW page, not the edit page

the request is created (or the draft updated), then submitted: masterStatus SUBMITTED, a document number YYYY-NNNN is issued, an audit log SUBMITTED is written, and the browser goes to the detail page

alternate_paths.name: No position on profile
alternate_paths.trigger: the requestor's profile has no position
alternate_paths.result: request.create refuses with FORBIDDEN naming the profile — the position is printed on the form and cannot be blank

alternate_paths.name: CREATE_REQUEST revoked
alternate_paths.result: assertPermission throws FORBIDDEN before anything is written

alternate_paths.name: Upload fails on save
alternate_paths.trigger: S3 rejects a file during the flush
alternate_paths.result: nothing is created, the form keeps its values and its files, and the error names which file failed

alternate_paths.name: Validation fails
alternate_paths.trigger: a required field is empty on submit
alternate_paths.result: the first invalid field is focused and no request is made — for both Save Draft and Submit, because a draft still has to be a valid record

trpc_procedures.name: create
guards: userId, requestedBy, position, targetOrg and responsibleOrg are all written server-side from the session, never from input
trpc_procedures.description: Creates a DRAFT and its CREATED audit log in one transaction. requestedBy is composed from the session's firstname + lastname; position comes from the session user, so the input copies are advisory only.

trpc_procedures.name: saveDraft
guards: masterStatus must be DRAFT or RETURNED
trpc_procedures.description: Updates an editable request in place. Writes no audit log — an edit is not a lifecycle event.

trpc_procedures.name: submit
guards: masterStatus must be DRAFT or RETURNED
trpc_procedures.description: Sets masterStatus SUBMITTED, issues a document number ONLY if one is not already set, and writes a SUBMITTED audit log — whose createdAt becomes the date and time printed on the PDF.

components.name: RequestForm
components.heroui_note: Typography per CLAUDE.md. Everything else is a lab component; the old AppForm field-array abstraction is dropped in favour of explicit fields, because the read-only mode needs per-field control the array config never gave it.
components.description: The whole form. Two columns on desktop: fields on the left, a side rail on the right holding processor, attachments, the status chip and the action buttons. In read-only mode every field renders through AppReadOnlyField rather than a disabled input — a disabled input still looks like something you failed to be allowed to type in.

components.name: AttachmentUploader
components.heroui_note: None. AppFileUpload brings the dashed dropzone, drag-and-drop, per-file progress, retry and remove — the four things IRMS-old listed as an open task and never built.
components.description: Multiple files, any type, capped by maxFiles and maxSizeBytes from src/lib/upload-constraints.ts. Uses useDeferredUpload('request-attachments'): dropping parks, saving sends. In read-only mode it becomes a plain download list.

components.name: WorkflowStepper
components.heroui_note: Typography per CLAUDE.md. AppStepper replaces the hand-rolled framer-motion timeline, its pulsing box-shadow animation and its own connector maths.
components.description: Seven steps: Draft, Submitted, IDO Evaluation, Director Review, IDO Final, Final Director, Completed. currentStep is derived from masterStatus; a returned or rejected request pins the marker at the stage it stopped and the label reads Returned or Rejected.

hooks.note: useRequestById — suspense query on request.getById, shared with specs 006 and 007.
create, saveDraft and submit, each wrapped in useUploadingSubmit so the flush → rewrite → save → release order cannot be got wrong at a call site.

functional: targetOrg and responsibleOrg are constants ('IDO'), stripped from the payload before it is sent and written server-side. They exist because the printed form has the fields, not because anyone chooses them.
Save Draft redirects to /requests/$requestId — the view page — not back to the edit page. The expectation is that the user then presses Edit Request deliberately (an explicit IRMS-old fix).
Submit from the create page performs create-then-submit in sequence; from an existing draft it performs saveDraft-then-submit, so unsaved edits are never lost by submitting.
The document number is issued once, on the first submit. A RETURNED request that is resubmitted keeps its original number.
Uploads are deferred: dropping a file parks it under an object URL and only the save flushes it, so files the user thought better of never reach the bucket.
'request-attachments' is added to UPLOAD_FOLDERS, and src/lib/image-urls.ts reports every attachment URL of every request or the sweep will delete live attachments.
The workflow stepper is visible in every mode, including create, where it correctly shows step 1 of 7.
The side rail shows Processor as 'Not yet assigned' until IDO recommends the request, with the caption saying who assigns it.
authorization: Server gate on create: ctx.user.position must be set, then assertPermission(CREATE_REQUEST). Both run before anything is written.
Server gate on saveDraft and submit: ownership (request.userId === ctx.user.id) AND an editable status. Staff have their own routes and must not be able to edit a requestor's text.
Ownership is checked against the session, never against a userId in the payload.
Editable statuses are exactly DRAFT and RETURNED. Anything else is FORBIDDEN, which is what stops a requestor rewriting a request that is already under review.
ux: Validation is on blur, re-validated on change once a field is wrong — the useAppForm default. Never validate while the user is still typing their first attempt.
Both buttons show a pending state and are disabled while either mutation runs, so a double press cannot create two requests.
The helper line under the buttons says what each does: submitting sends it to IDO, saving lets you finish later.
Attachments show real byte progress during the flush. A silent pause between pressing Submit and the redirect is the worst version of this screen.
Read-only mode uses AppReadOnlyField, not disabled inputs.
Required fields are marked on the label, not only by the error that appears after the fact.

rules.zod_rule: z.array(attachmentSchema) where attachmentSchema = z.object({ url: storedImageUrl(), name: z.string().min(1) })

edge_cases: Submit from the create page is two mutations. If the submit half fails, a DRAFT already exists — do not retry create on the retry, and take the user to the draft rather than leaving them on a form whose data is already saved.

requestedBy and position arrive in the payload but the server rewrites both from the session; treat the input copies as display values only, or a crafted payload files a request in someone else's name.
attachments is a Json column, so nothing at the database level guarantees its shape — the Zod array is the only guard and it must run on the server too.
A flush that half-succeeds leaves some files in the bucket and no row pointing at them. That is what s3:sweep is for; do not attempt inline cleanup on failure.
Draft validation is full validation. A draft that skips required fields becomes a submitted request that skips them, because submit only checks status.
The stepper's index map must cover every masterStatus including the terminal rejections, or a rejected request renders with currentStep -1 and no marker at all.
out_of_scope: Editing an existing request — spec 007, same component in edit mode.
The comment thread — spec 008; it is not mounted on the create page because there is nothing to comment on yet.
Rich text in Details — the printed form is plain text and a rich body would not survive it.
